onsager_critical_minus_beta_f.cite: -beta f = ln Z / N of the square-lattice Ising model at beta_c J = (1/2) ln(1 + sqrt 2), zero field: (1/2) ln 2 + 2G/pi, G Catalan's constant. OEIS A242743 (page read: 'Decimal expansion of an Ising constant', formula log(2)/2 + 2*G/Pi, 105 digits 0.929695398341610214985384973665878121765882375151802..., comment: the negated ratio of free energy per node to the temperature at the critical point; references Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944), Eq. (121) (not fetched) and Finch, Mathematical Constants (2003), Sec. 5.22 (not fetched)). Concordant: Caselle & Hasenbusch, arXiv:hep-th/9911216 (search-engine excerpt only, f_b = 2G/pi + (1/2) log 2 = 0.9296953982...; PDF not read). beta_c_square.cite: critical point of the square-lattice Ising model with J = 1, beta_c = (1/2) ln(1 + sqrt 2): Kramers & Wannier, Phys. Rev. 60, 252 (1941) and Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944) (both not fetched); read from Duminil-Copin, '100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice', arXiv:2208.00864v1 (2022), PDF read: Sec. 3.1, after Eq. (3.3) ('beta_c must be equal to (1/2) ln(1 + sqrt 2)'). Value: (1/2) ln(1 + sqrt 2) evaluated by mpmath at 50 digits, rounded to 30 places; tol 1e-29
beta_c_square.independent_route: replicant's certified ball (1/2) log(1 + sqrt 2) in arb (lattice/onsager.critical_beta); the transition is also where sinh(2 beta) = 1, the edge of Yang's formula (Duminil-Copin Eq. (3.7)), checked by the refusal of yang_magnetization just below it (tests/test_lattice.py)

yang_exponent.cite: spontaneous magnetization of the square-lattice Ising model, m*(beta) = (1 - sinh(2 beta)^-4)^(1/8) for beta >= beta_c (J = 1): Yang, Phys. Rev. 85, 808 (1952) (not fetched); read from Duminil-Copin, arXiv:2208.00864v1 (2022), PDF read: Sec. 3.2, Eq. (3.7). The exponent beta = 1/8 of m* ~ (beta - beta_c)^(1/8). tol 1e-5: the band of the finite-difference log-log slope at beta - beta_c = 1e-6, 1e-8 (the O(beta - beta_c) correction is below 2e-7, the band excludes 1/4 and 1/16)
yang_exponent.independent_route: none independent of the cited formula: the log-log slope of replicant's certified balls of Eq. (3.7) at two distances from beta_c (lattice/onsager.yang_loglog_slope), a consistency check of the implementation, not a derivation of the exponent

bethe_beta_c_k3.cite: ferromagnetic Ising model on the random 3-regular graph / Bethe lattice of coordination 3: the critical point rho tanh beta_c = 1 with rho = k - 1 = 2 the branching factor, i.e. beta_c = atanh(1/2): Dembo & Montanari, 'Ising models on locally tree-like graphs', Ann. Appl. Probab. 20 (2010) 565, doi:10.1214/09-AAP627, arXiv:0804.4726v3, PDF read: Sec. 2.2, Eq. (2.5) (stated there as the statistical-physics prediction; the paragraph 'Random regular graphs' gives rho = k - 1 for degree k). Value: atanh(1/2) = (1/2) ln 3 by mpmath at 50 digits, rounded to 30 places; tol 1e-29
bethe_beta_c_k3.independent_route: replicant's certified count of the BP fixed points (lattice/bethe.py): one fixed point at beta = 0.54, three at beta = 0.56 (interval Newton in arb on each monotone interval of the cavity equation), and the certified BP Jacobian (k - 1) xi'(0) = 2 tanh beta crossing 1 (tests/test_lattice.py)

ising1d_minus_beta_f_beta1_h0.cite: one-dimensional Ising model, J = 1: -beta f = ln lambda_1, lambda_1 = e^{beta J}[cosh(beta h) + sqrt(sinh^2(beta h) + e^{-4 beta J})]: Wang, Diaz-Mendez & Capdevila, 'Solving the one-dimensional Ising chain via mathematical induction: an intuitive approach to the transfer matrix', arXiv:1907.11701 (ar5iv HTML read; journal reference not checked), Eqs. (1), (4), (6), (7) (Z_N = Tr P^N = lambda_1^N + lambda_2^N), (9), (12); concordant: Wikipedia, 'Ising model', Sec. One dimension (read); the textbook source Baxter, Exactly Solved Models in Statistical Mechanics (1982), Ch. 2, was not fetched. At beta = 1, h = 0: -beta f = ln(e + e^-1) = ln(2 cosh 1), a formula evaluation at a chosen point (mpmath, 50 digits, rounded to 30 places); tol 1e-29
ising1d_minus_beta_f_beta1_h0.independent_route: the exact identity Z_N = Tr T^N = lambda_+^N + lambda_-^N on rings of N = 2 .. 10 spins at rational e^K, e^{beta h}: brute-force enumeration of the 2^N configurations, the exact rational transfer-matrix trace and the closed form in Q(sqrt D) (lattice/transfer.ising1d_ring_identity), and replicant's certified ball of ln lambda_+ (tests/test_lattice.py)

ising1d_magnetization_beta1_h1_2.cite: one-dimensional Ising model, J = 1, beta = 1, h = 1/2 (K = 1, Baxter's h = beta h = 1/2): M = e^K sinh h / [e^{2K} sinh^2 h + e^{-2K}]^{1/2}, Baxter, Exactly Solved Models in Statistical Mechanics (Academic Press, 1982), Ch. 2 (PDF read: physics.anu.edu.au/research/ftp/_files/Exactly.pdf, book pp. 16-20 and 32-38), Eq. onsager_critical_energy.cite: internal energy per site U/N of the square-lattice Ising model at beta_c, J = 1: Onsager, 'Crystal Statistics. I.', Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944), doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117 (journal scan read, www.phys.ens.psl.eu/~langlois/Onsager43.pdf, pp. 140-143), Eq. (121): '-U_c/NJ = 2^{1/2} = 1.414 213 56' (the limit of Eq. (116), U = -NJ coth 2H (1 + (2/pi) k1'' K1), at k1'' = 0: 'the energy is continuous because k1'' = 0'). Value: -sqrt 2 by mpmath at 60 digits, rounded to 30 places; tol 1e-29
onsager_critical_energy.independent_route: replicant's certified Eq. (116) at beta_c +- 1e-30 (lattice/onsager_thermo.py, agm/elliptic in arb) and the derivative of Onsager's single integral under the integral sign (acb.integral) off beta_c; the L x L torus energy from Kaufman's Z (K-derivative by arb_series) approaches it as L grows (-1.4166 at L = 256, gap ~ 1/L; tests/test_lattice_obs.py)

onsager_specific_heat_amplitude.cite: coefficient A of the logarithmic divergence of the specific heat of the square-lattice Ising model, C/Nk = -A ln|K - K_c| + O(1) on both sides of beta_c: Onsager, 'Crystal Statistics. I.', Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944), doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117 (journal scan read, www.phys.ens.psl.eu/~langlois/Onsager43.pdf, pp. 140-143), Eq. (120): 'K1 ~ log(4/k1') ~ log(2^{1/2}/|H - H_c|), C/Nk ~ (2/pi)(log cot pi/8)^2 (K1 - 1 - pi/4)', so A = (2/pi) ln^2 cot(pi/8) = (2/pi) ln^2(1 + sqrt 2); Onsager's finite-width maximum, Eq. (127), '0.4945 log n + 0.1879', carries the same coefficient (4 digits). Concordance note: Baxter, Exactly Solved Models (1982), Sec. 7.12, Eqs. (7.12.3)-(7.12.7) (PDF read) give the singular free energy; as printed, (7.12.7) has (1 + k) in the numerator where (7.12.3) with (7.12.6) gives it in the denominator, a factor 4 at k = 1; Onsager's (120) and (127) and replicant's certified Eq. (117) agree with the denominator form. Value: mpmath at 60 digits, rounded to 30 places; tol 1e-29
onsager_specific_heat_amplitude.independent_route: replicant's certified log-slope [c(beta_c + 1e-8) - c(beta_c + 1e-6)] / ln 100 of Onsager's Eq. (117) (|slope - A| = 4.3e-7, both sides; the band 1e-5 excludes 4/pi ln^2(1 + sqrt 2)); the L x L torus at beta_c from Kaufman's Z (arb_series): (c_2L - c_L)/ln 2 - A = 1.9e-3, 9.6e-4 at L = 64 -> 128 -> 256 (observed ~ 0.246/L), Richardson in 1/L within 2.7e-6 of A (finite-size sequence, a consistency check; tests/test_lattice_obs.py)

ising2d_correlation_length_beta0_3.cite: exponential correlation length along a lattice axis of the isotropic square-lattice Ising model (J = 1, K = beta), K* the dual coupling, sinh 2K sinh 2K* = 1 (Onsager, 'Crystal Statistics. I.', Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944), doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117 (journal scan read, www.phys.ens.psl.eu/~langlois/Onsager43.pdf, pp. 117, 137-138, as page images), Eq. (17)). Strip spectrum: Eqs. (89a), (95), (97)-(100) (gamma_0 = 2|K - K*|); the limit of the ratio of the two largest eigenvalues, Eq. (101), and 'the range ... is inversely proportional to log(lambda_max/lambda)' (p. 138). Discrepancy: (101) prints exp(2H* - 2H') for lambda^(-)/lambda when H' < H*, which exceeds 1; Eqs. (99), (100) give exp(2H' - 2H*). T > T_c: 1/xi = 2(K* - K) at K = 0.3. Value: mpmath at 60 digits of the formula, rounded to 31 significant digits; tol 1e-29
ising2d_correlation_length_beta0_3.independent_route: Onsager's strip gaps at widths 4 and 6 equal the direct double-precision diagonalisation of the strip transfer matrix (lattice/strip_tm.py, to 1e-9); the width-256 gap lambda_0/lambda_1 is within 1e-36 of the bulk value (exponential convergence; a finite-size check, tests/test_lattice_xi.py)

ising2d_correlation_length_beta0_6.cite: exponential correlation length along a lattice axis of the isotropic square-lattice Ising model (J = 1, K = beta), K* the dual coupling, sinh 2K sinh 2K* = 1 (Onsager, 'Crystal Statistics. I.', Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944), doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117 (journal scan read, www.phys.ens.psl.eu/~langlois/Onsager43.pdf, pp. 117, 137-138, as page images), Eq. (17)). Strip spectrum: Eqs. (89a), (95), (97)-(100) (gamma_0 = 2|K - K*|); the limit of the ratio of the two largest eigenvalues, Eq. (101), and 'the range ... is inversely proportional to log(lambda_max/lambda)' (p. 138). Discrepancy: (101) prints exp(2H* - 2H') for lambda^(-)/lambda when H' < H*, which exceeds 1; Eqs. (99), (100) give exp(2H' - 2H*). T < T_c: lambda_0, lambda_1 are asymptotically degenerate (Eqs. (101), (103)); the next level of the principal sector is log lambda_max - 2 gamma_1 (Eq. (102)), so 1/xi = 2 gamma(0) = 4(K - K*) at K = 0.6. The identification of the two-particle gap with the decay of the connected correlation is taken from the form-factor expansions of Lyberg & McCoy, arXiv:math-ph/0612051 (PDF read), Eqs. (5), (13), (20), (21) (even terms below T_c, z^N factors per particle, branch points at alpha_2 = e^{-2K} coth K): the derivation of the decay rate alpha_2^{2N} is replicant's; concordant near T_c with Dohm, arXiv:1907.00859, Eqs. (41), (46): xi_0+ = 2 xi_0-. Value: mpmath at 60 digits, 31 significant digits; tol 1e-29
ising2d_correlation_length_beta0_6.independent_route: Onsager's strip gaps equal the direct transfer matrix at widths 4, 6; Richardson in 1/n^2 of the lambda_0/lambda_2 gap at widths 64, 128, 256 is within 1.3e-7 of the bulk value (band 5.8e-6; the T > T_c branch 2(K - K*) = 0.578 is excluded); a finite-size consistency check, tests/test_lattice_xi.py

ising2d_correlation_length_amplitude_plu.cite: xi = xi_0+ t^-1 (t = T/T_c - 1 -> 0+) for the isotropic square-lattice Ising model: Dohm, arXiv:1907.00859v3 (2019) (PDF read), Eq. (30): xi_0+ = (4 beta_c E)^-1 = [2 ln(1 + 2^{1/2})]^-1, from Wu, McCoy, Tracy & Barouch, Phys. Rev. B 13, 316 (1976) (not fetched). Value: 60-digit mpmath, rounded; tol 1e-11 covers the O(t) of replicant's evaluation xi |t| at K - K_c = -1e-12 (measured 8.9e-13)
ising2d_correlation_length_amplitude_plu.independent_route: xi |t| of replicant's certified exact form 1/xi = 2(K* - K) (Onsager's gap) at K - K_c = -1e-12 (catalog value correlation_length_amplitude_plus)

ising2d_correlation_length_amplitude_rat.cite: xi_0+ / xi_0- = 2 for the exponential correlation lengths of the 2D Ising model: Dohm, arXiv:1907.00859v3 (PDF read), Eqs. (41), (46) and the text after Eq. (14) ('xi_0+/xi_0- = 2'); tol 1e-11 covers the O(t) of the evaluation at K - K_c = -+1e-12
ising2d_correlation_length_amplitude_rat.independent_route: ratio of replicant's xi |t| above and below T_c from the exact forms 2(K* - K), 4(K - K*)

ising2d_critical_nn_correlation.cite: <s_0 s_1> for nearest neighbours of the square-lattice Ising model at T_c: -u_c/(2J) with Onsager, 'Crystal Statistics. I.', Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944), doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117 (journal scan read, www.phys.ens.psl.eu/~langlois/Onsager43.pdf, pp. 117, 137-138, as page images), Eq. (121): -U_c/NJ = 2^{1/2} (pp. 140-143, read in I1); two bonds per site and isotropy give u = -2J <s s'>_nn, so sqrt 2 / 2 (the step from u to the bond correlation is replicant's). Value: 31 digits of sqrt 2 / 2; tol 1e-29
ising2d_critical_nn_correlation.independent_route: on the periodic strip of width L = 3 .. 8 at beta_c the mean of the row and column nearest-neighbour correlations (direct transfer matrix, principal eigenvector, double precision) equals sqrt 2 / 2 to 1e-15 (an observed identity, not proved here; tests/test_lattice_xi.py)

ising2d_critical_diagonal_correlation_n1.cite: <s_{0,0} s_{1,1}> at T_c = 2/pi: Perk & Au-Yang, arXiv:0901.1931v3 (PDF read), Eqs. (31), (32) (k = 1: r_1 = log(2/pi)); Deift, Its & Krasovsky, arXiv:1207.4990v3 (PDF read), Eqs. (103)-(105): the Toeplitz determinant of the symbol e^{i(pi - theta)/2}, coefficients (2/pi)/(2k + 1), whose 1 x 1 case is 2/pi. Value: 31 digits; tol 1e-29

ising2d_critical_diagonal_amplitude.cite: <s_{1,1} s_{1+n,1+n}> = e^{1/4} 2^{1/12} A^{-3} n^{-1/4} (1 - 1/(64 n^2) + ...) at T = T_c, A Glaisher's constant: Deift, Its & Krasovsky, arXiv:1207.4990v3 (PDF read), Eqs. ising2d_strip_critical_gap_amplitude.cite: lim n ln(lambda_0/lambda_1) at beta_c on the periodic strip of width n = 2 pi x_sigma = pi eta = pi/4: Cardy, 'Conformal Field Theory and Statistical Mechanics', arXiv:0807.3472 (PDF read), Eq. (19) (H = (2 pi/L)(L_0 + Lbar_0 - c/12): gap 2 pi x / L) and Sec. 2 (<phi phi> = |r|^{-2x}); eta = 1/4 from the decay n^{-1/4} at T_c, Deift, Its & Krasovsky, arXiv:1207.4990, Eq. (101) (Fisher 1959). The isotropic lattice needs no anisotropy factor. Note: the I2 brief's 'L xi_L^-1 -> pi eta / 2' is a factor 2 below this; the data (Onsager's strip gaps: 0.78541788 at n = 128) give pi/4. Value: 31 digits of pi/4; tol 1e-29
ising2d_strip_critical_gap_amplitude.independent_route: Onsager's certified strip gaps n ln(lambda_0/lambda_1) at beta_c: Richardson in 1/n^2 at n = 128, 256 is within 7.4e-10 of pi/4 (band 1e-8); direct transfer matrix agrees at n = 4, 6
